turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select 5 candidates that jointly span the best
trade-off between a LARGE SHG tensor component |d_ij| and a WIDE band gap.
Neither is given for the pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated
hypervolume they span in the normalized (|d_ij|, band gap) plane, so a set
of mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5
candidates that are all strong on the same single axis.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would select **c030, c070, c055, c051, and c057** as a frontier-covering set. This is a **structure-informed prediction**, not a claim that their unknown properties have been calculated or that they are guaranteed to be mutually non-dominated.

The training data favor three complementary regions: strongly polarizable tellurides/arsenides for large SHG, ordered tetrahedral sulfides for the middle of the trade-off, and light-element sulfides for wider gaps. They also show why structural matching matters: different polymorphs can have very different SHG despite identical composition.

| Rank | Candidate | Structural reasoning and training-data support | Intended frontier role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030 — CdSiP₂** | The POSCAR has the ordered, non-centrosymmetric **chalcopyrite tetrahedral framework**. Its close structural analogue ZnSiP₂ gives **51.4 pm/V, 2.11 eV** in training. Cd adds polarizability, while the Si–P framework makes this a stronger balanced prospect than many heavy-element, narrow-gap compounds. | **Main SHG–gap compromise** |
| **2** | **c070 — Cu₃TaTe₄** | A **sulvanite-type tetrahedral structure**, with Ta at the origin, Cu on the three half-axis sites, and Te on a tetrahedral positional orbit. This cubic arrangement permits SHG; cubic symmetry alone does not imply inversion symmetry. The polarizable Cu–Te framework makes it a promising high-SHG endpoint. Training tellurides such as ZnGa₂Te₄ and CdGa₂Te₄ reach approximately **92 pm/V at 1.6–1.7 eV**, although those are chemical rather than exact structural analogues. | **High-SHG endpoint; higher uncertainty** |
| **3** | **c055 — AlGaAs₂** | The hexagonal cell contains an **ordered [111]-stacked tetrahedral semiconductor framework**, rather than an arbitrary low-symmetry arrangement. Al incorporation offers a route to a wider gap than a Ga-rich arsenide, while As retains substantial electronic polarizability. Training AlGaP₂ versus GaP illustrates the relevant Al-induced trade-off: **35.5 pm/V, 2.31 eV** versus **61.3 pm/V, 2.05 eV** for cubic GaP. | **Bridge between the SHG endpoint and balanced phosphide** |
| **4** | **c051 — ZnGa₂S₄** | Its cation/vacancy ordering and anion coordinates closely follow the **defect-chalcopyrite family** represented by training CdGa₂S₄ (**21.7 pm/V, 2.86 eV**). Zn substitution is a plausible way to extend the gap while retaining appreciable tetrahedral-network SHG. I prefer this structurally supported candidate over treating all three ZnGa₂S₄ polymorphs as interchangeable. | **Wider-gap, moderate-SHG region** |
| **5** | **c057 — LiAlS₂** | The orthorhombic structure closely resembles training orthorhombic LiGaSe₂. Replacing Ga/Se with Al/S should favor a wider gap, at the cost of SHG. Training Al₂S₃ (**4.75 pm/V, 3.88 eV**) and Li₂SiS₃ (**4.85 pm/V, 4.29 eV**) support this light-element-sulfide strategy. | **Wide-gap endpoint with useful residual SHG** |

I would **not spend a slot solely on the widest-gap ionic halide**: the training halides commonly provide only about 0.1–1 pm/V, so their additional dominated area can be small. Likewise, selecting several closely related selenide polymorphs would risk concentrating all five picks in the same part of the plane.

Final: c030, c070, c055, c051, c057
